item.description:
Background Innovations have improved outcomes in high-risk localised, locally advanced, and biochemically recurrent prostate cancer (PC), yet high-level evidence remains limited for many management decisions. The 2026 Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference (APCCC) surveyed an international panel on key clinical questions to complement evidence-based guidelines. Objective Here we present the voting results for the questions on high-risk localised, locally advanced, and biochemically recurrent PC from APCCC 2026. item.title: Treatment Effect of Perioperative (Neoadjuvant and Adjuvant) Apalutamide plus Androgen-deprivation Therapy Versus Radical Prostatectomy Alone in Patients with High-risk Localized or Locally Advanced Prostate Cancer from the PROTEUS Substudy.
item.author: Briganti A, Steuber T, Shore ND, Gleave M, Kretschmer A, Wetherhold L, Efstathiou E, Cahn DJ, Damião R, De La Taille A, Byun SS, Hadaschik BA, Imbroda BH, Soto ÁJ, Merseburger AS, Simone G, Rooney B, Mikerin D, Li Z, Miladinovic B, McCarthy SA, Wildgust M, Mundle SD, Kibel AS, Taplin ME.
item.description:
The blinded placebo-controlled PROTEUS (Perioperative Treatment with Erleada United with Surgery) study demonstrated that adding 1-yr perioperative apalutamide plus androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT) benefited patients with high-risk localized prostate cancer or locally advanced prostate cancer (HR-LPC/LAPC) who were undergoing radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection (RP). This substudy evaluated 1-yr perioperative apalutamide plus ADT versus standard-of-care (SOC) RP. Patients with newly diagnosed HR-LPC/LAPC were randomized 1:3 to open-label perioperative apalutamide (240 mg/d) plus ADT (six 28-d cycles before and after RP) or RP. The primary end point was event-free survival (EFS), defined as time to biochemical failure, local/regional recurrence, distant metastasis, or death. Context There are substantial regional differences in prostate cancer (PCa) epidemiology reflecting differences in risk factors, screening, management, and access to care. Objective To assess geographical differences and temporal trends in PCa incidence and mortality and PCa risk factors. Evidence acquisition Estimated incidence and mortality data for the year 2024 and projections to 2050 based on the assumption that 2024 age-specific incidence and mortality rates remain unchanged (not accounting for changes in risk factors and/or treatments) in 185 countries were derived from the International Agency for Research on Cancer's GLOBOCAN 2024 database. item.title: Surgery in Motion: Different Surgical Techniques for Inguinal Lymph Node Dissection in Penile Cancer.
item.author: Verdijk RWA, Patterson K, Brassetti A, Fankhauser C, Albersen M, Muneer A, Parnham A, Brouwer OR.
item.description:
Inguinal lymph node dissection (ILND) remains a cornerstone of nodal management in penile cancer, providing definitive treatment for clinically node-positive disease and surgical staging for high-risk clinically node-negative patients when dynamic sentinel node biopsy (DSNB) is unavailable. Despite its oncological importance, ILND is associated with substantial morbidity. Over the past decade, minimally invasive (MI) approaches have emerged as alternatives to open ILND, with the potential to reduce wound-related complications while maintaining oncological efficacy. This Surgery in Motion article provides a practical overview of contemporary open, video-endoscopic (VEIL), and robot-assisted (RAVEIL) ILND techniques, integrating anatomical principles, technical variations, and current clinical evidence. item.description:
Background and objective Prospective proteomic and proteogenomic studies may enhance the understanding of proteins associated with prostate cancer (PCa) development. Methods In a case-cohort study within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC), baseline plasma samples from 982 incident PCa cases and 1573 subcohort participants were profiled using the SomaScan 7k platform (over 6000 proteins). Associations were estimated using Prentice-weighted Cox models. The coprimary end points were incident overall PCa and aggressive PCa (n = 290). Findings were evaluated in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) study and supported by Mendelian randomization (MR) and exome gene-burden analyses.
